stories.headline: Zelensky says US focus is too much on Middle East
stories.summary: Ukraine's president told the BBC the US is too focused on the Middle East and not pressing Russia hard enough. He called it "strange" that Trump has described Vladimir Putin as a friend. Separately, Trump said he had urged Putin to 'pull back' military aggression in Europe, as Zelenskyy warned of a major Russian attack.

stories.headline: Thanksgiving storms cause outages and flight delays across US
stories.summary: Almost one million US customers had no power on Thursday evening as storms hit both coasts with wind gusts, heavy rain and flooding. Roofs were torn off and streets flooded, with hundreds of thousands affected as the holiday weekend began. Flight delays were reported and coastal flooding was a concern.

stories.headline: New Zealand coalition loses majority; Opportunity Party holds key role
stories.summary: Final results show Christopher Luxon's right-leaning coalition, led by the National Party, is one seat short of a majority. It now needs the support of the centrist newcomer Opportunity Party to govern, or the country faces another election. The Opportunity Party is now positioned to swing the next parliament left or right.

stories.headline: Two Italians killed in Kuwait strike; Iran denies responsibility
stories.summary: Two Italians, technicians for German company Rheinmetall according to Italy's foreign ministry, were killed in a strike in Kuwait. Iran denies responsibility, and Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi called the incident "suspicious". Trump said the Iran war ends "whenever I want it".

stories.headline: Congo Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 cases
stories.summary: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo has reached 12,000 cases and continues to spread quickly. Fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting containment efforts, and some responders have been evacuated.

stories.headline: North Korea's Kim vows more nuclear weapons
stories.summary: Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities producing nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons. He made the call after ignoring a Trump overture, citing threats from the US and South Korea.

stories.headline: Egyptian motorist arrested over tanker crash that killed 31
stories.summary: Egyptian authorities arrested a motorist over a tanker crash that killed 31 people. Officials say he confessed to speeding and clipping the fuel truck while overtaking.

stories.headline: Mortgage payments set to rise for hundreds of thousands
stories.summary: The Bank of England warns that more than 400,000 UK homeowners will face a rise of £500 or more a month in mortgage payments over the next three years as they come off fixed deals. Another report says millions will see average monthly payments rise by £100.

stories.headline: Altria considers takeover bid for Imperial Brands
stories.summary: US tobacco group Altria has announced it is considering a possible takeover bid for UK firm Imperial Brands. Imperial shares jumped more than 14% on the news. Imperial could become the next UK company to fall to a foreign takeover.

stories.headline: Pablo Hernández de Cos chosen as next ECB president
stories.summary: Former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos has been chosen to succeed Christine Lagarde at the European Central Bank. He won support from the EU's biggest countries.

stories.headline: Tech stocks and Nvidia drive volatile markets
stories.summary: Tech stocks were set for their worst month in four years as volatility surged, according to the FT. Asian markets rallied after the tech rout, and Chinese shares soared after Beijing signalled more support. Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO brought some relief to the AI trade.

stories.headline: Poundland's collapse and owner blame
stories.summary: Poundland's management and MPs blame its owners Gordon Brothers, but the US firm says the chain would have collapsed last year without them. Staff fear being left without work before Christmas. Travelodge has appointed a new chief executive from 1 December.

stories.headline: Norse Atlantic suspends all flights
stories.summary: Norse Atlantic has suspended all flights as it faces potential collapse. The carrier is seeking urgent funding and will file for bankruptcy without a financial lifeline.

stories.headline: US GDP revision prompts Trump probe demand
stories.summary: Trump demanded an investigation into a 'record setting error' after third-quarter GDP data was revised sharply higher. He said the revision should be "immediately investigated".

stories.headline: Aston Villa: Garnacho's career looks stalled
stories.summary: Alejandro Garnacho's brief Aston Villa career already looks over, as he did not make a 12-man bench. Villa lost to Galatasaray in the Champions League earlier this week.

stories.headline: Man Utd and Sporting draw 2-2; Lammens under scrutiny
stories.summary: Manchester United drew 2-2 with Sporting in the Champions League. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens made two major mistakes and is under scrutiny ahead of the weekend.

stories.headline: Pant plays club match in New Zealand under false name
stories.summary: India wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant joined a club game in Christchurch under the false name 'Stan Stan' before the second Test. He scored 54 off 21 balls.

stories.headline: Lyon set to be dropped for first New Zealand Test
stories.summary: Nathan Lyon is set to be axed from Australia's squad for the first Test against New Zealand in Perth. The 39-year-old's omission raises questions over his red-ball future.

stories.headline: Cricket Australia widens sandpapergate probe
stories.summary: Cricket Australia's independent forum into sandpapergate will include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England. The forum will be confidential and led by Fiona McLeod, with no sanctions and no recrimination.

stories.headline: Faldo urges LIV stars to pay unpaid firms; Lee opens with 68
stories.summary: Six-time major winner Nick Faldo urged LIV Golf stars who benefited financially to help small businesses still owed money. Min Woo Lee shot a four-under 68 in the first round of the Australian PGA Championship despite missing his eight-iron.

stories.headline: Lenacapavir HIV prevention jab reaches Africa
stories.summary: A cheaper HIV prevention jab, lenacapavir, has reached Africa. It is given as an injection twice a year and is nearly 100% effective at preventing HIV infection.

stories.headline: Musk's million-satellite plan approved
stories.summary: US approval has been given for SpaceX's plan to send a million data satellites into space, called the Starmind constellation. It aims to be the most cost and energy-efficient way to meet growing demand for AI computing power.

stories.headline: UK cement and lime industry calls for carbon capture support
stories.summary: UK cement and lime producers have joined major trade unions and parliamentarians in calling on the government for carbon capture support. Separately, ARK Capture Solutions raised more than €5.4 million in seed funding to scale all-electric carbon capture.

stories.headline: Depardieu to stand trial for alleged rape
stories.summary: Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial in Paris for the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018, after an appeals court rejected his attempt to avoid it. Arnould first made the accusation in 2018.

stories.headline: Huw Edwards gives first interviews since conviction
stories.summary: Huw Edwards has given his first interviews since his conviction for child abuse image offences. Minister Anna Turley said she was "deeply uncomfortable" with the interviews, while Channel 4 insisted it "holds Edwards to account".

stories.headline: Tributes for Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor and King Crimson drummer Michael Giles
stories.summary: Tributes have been paid to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor, who died aged 65. Bandmate Simon Le Bon said Taylor "brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music". King Crimson co-founder and drummer Michael Giles has also died, aged 84.

stories.headline: Government antisemitism adviser probes BBC
stories.summary: Lord Mann has launched an investigation into the BBC after what he describes as "growing discomfort among Jewish BBC staff". The BBC was not quoted in the items.

stories.headline: Baby with brain cancer makes full recovery
stories.summary: An infant girl given weeks to live from aggressive brain cancer has made a full recovery. Her case reached a hospital that had just finished a study on her type of cancer, and the trial had run at St. Jude Children's Hospital.

stories.headline: Texans farm free to fund college scholarships
stories.summary: Texas residents have spent 15 years farming land not their own for free to raise money for college scholarships. The tradition has paid out $3 million to hundreds of high school students.

stories.headline: Floating nature islands for Glasgow parks
stories.summary: Floating nature islands are being planted in five Glasgow parks as part of the Glasgow Games legacy. They are designed to encourage wildlife and help clean the water.

stories.headline: Waterstones prize for father and son's cut-out book
stories.summary: A father and son from Bristol have won a Waterstones book prize for their cut-out picture book, described as "picture-book perfection".

stories.headline: Solo dining becomes a self-care trend
stories.summary: Dining alone is being embraced as a self-care trend and is reshaping the restaurant industry. One writer says they spend £200 a month on fancy meals by themselves.
